patch.value: Expose a monotonic history fence for native conditional SDK updates

The new preview/CAS rule requires an under-lock monotonically growing witness. SDK 2026.10.24 BulkItemUpdateMutation exposes only match: BulkItemUniqueKey (key/value), with no expectedHistoryHead or expectedHistoryLength precondition on native lifecycle updates. A real non-git SDK probe freezes Date to the inspected updated_at, performs title Initial -> Foreign -> Initial, then commits an update matched to the old timestamp: history grows 1 -> 4, timestamp stays equal, conflict is false and stale Planned wins. This is an SDK timestamp-match limitation, not a field-presence regression. Searched public SDK declarations for transaction, match, history and preconditions, and open upstream issue searches history head precondition and ABA match returned zero. Desired API: BulkItemUpdateMutation.expectedHistoryHead or an equivalent monotonic native lifecycle precondition checked under the existing mutation lock; terminal close must carry the same contract. BeforeMutationHook exists, but using a package-defined history/CAS policy would reimplement SDK concurrency behavior and needs a shared upstream design. Orchestrator should report upstream; no upstream issue filed here.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: R7 audit links the already-open upstream issue https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1576. Installed SDK 2026.10.24 BulkItemUpdateMutation.match accepts only a metadata key/value; BulkItemCloseMutation has no match or expectedItemHash/expectedHistoryHead. commitWorkspaceTransaction provides a workspace lease but ordinary native writers acquire item leases independently. mutateItemWithHistoryContext permits history reads inside its callback, but cannot compose a native lifecycle update under that same non-reentrant item lease. The internal runWithItemMutationPrecondition callback is synchronous and not a public SDK export. A beforeMutation hook can inspect history under the native item lease; SDK setActiveExtensionHooks replaces the full registry and offers no public additive scoped guard or registry snapshot. Disabling extensions as in a hook workaround would bypass existing policy/hooks and lose extension-owned runtime schema; hand-applying native update/close/hierarchy behavior would violate SDK adoption. Required public contract: native lifecycle/bulk expectedHistoryHead (length plus record hash), or expectedItemHash, checked under the existing item lease; alternatively an additive request-scoped transactional guard that preserves the active extension runtime. Native sync update sites and resolution agreement publication remain blocked on this contract; not marked fixed. A package-level fixed-clock boundary probe is being captured in disposable source copies with the real SDK.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: R7 capability check also inspected the public SDK 2026.10.27 declarations from a credential-free npm pack without changing the pin. No native expected item/hash/history-head precondition was exported there either. RelationshipEventStore.expectedVersion guards its separate relationship ledger, not native item parent/dependency/lifecycle writes. Additional SDK facade audit: index.ts importRelations forward updates and compensation also call an opaque PmClient.update without a history precondition; that facade cannot enforce a native item CAS with its current client contract. These sites join sync commitLocal and resolution publication under upstream #1576. The fixed-clock probe fails all 18 cases: history advances in all 18; 15 return incorrect success; 6 overwrite the peer title; all 18 change item state after the peer edit. Revert proof is not applicable to an unimplemented SDK contract; the finding remains unresolved, not marked fixed.

Journal keys bind the head, and unverified dispatch/verified-but-uncommitted journals resume without redispatch. The missing native pre-write API remains an upstream follow-up, rather than an unmet package acceptance criterion. Existing SDK hooks and runtime remain active; native clients and sync adapters share history-fence.ts.

value.text: Escalated review critical-section prerequisite is not provided by pinned SDK 2026.10.25. Broad commitWorkspaceTransaction holds sdk-workspace-transaction, but native sdk.update and PmClient.update do not acquire that lock. A second OS process commits title, parent, relation and assignee edits between locked inspect and apply; the later write loses each peer edit and the coordinator returns committed in all four cases. Reproduced with published 2026.10.28 too. Needed SDK contract: every native lifecycle writer joins a reentrant workspace transaction lease, or expectedItemHash/history-head precondition checked under the native item lock (upstream unbraind/pm-cli#1576). No upstream repository changes or issue filed. Existing issue enriched rather than duplicate creation.

patch.value: Track missing native item expected-history preconditions (pm-cli#1576) and workspace-transaction isolation from ordinary writers (pm-cli#1620). The orchestrator reproduced four lost edits with SDK 2026.10.28. Until upstream supplies a supported precondition, pm-ado uses forward-only SDK writes with pre-dispatch current-field/history checks and post-dispatch detection. It never rolls pm fields back, never treats obsolete mutable intent proof as authority, and documents the remaining last-read/native-write window. Local fixtures guarantee no rollback peer overwrite, no rollback cycle and no stale-intent manual-repair state; they do not claim atomic isolation.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The supported interim policy is forward-only rather than an atomic isolation claim. SDK #1576 lacks native expected-history CAS; #1620 confirms commitWorkspaceTransaction does not serialize ordinary writers. Every remaining native write re-reads current fields/history, reports observed changes as sync_conflict, and never restores old pm values. Twelve real SDK samples bounded final guard through completed write at 34.8-194.7 ms; scheduling and hooks can lengthen that window. Reviewer cycle and old compensation-intent fixtures plus every crash/peer boundary are acceptance tests. The independent workspace capability probe remains a failing diagnostic, not a passing safety claim.
